exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean delivery, vaginal delivery, spontaneous vaginal delivery, elective Cesarean delivery, emergency Cesarean delivery, operative vaginal delivery)
cohort: 67,613 children from 9 European birth cohorts enrolled between 1996 and 2006
finding: Elective Cesarean delivery, compared to vaginal delivery, was associated with an increased risk of asthma at school age, particularly in children born at term.
mod_finding: Elective Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of asthma compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery, while emergency Cesarean delivery and operative vaginal delivery were not.
